_why:
Twenty-five cap-0 codes whose `whoThisIsFor` addressed a foreign reader with no denial anywhere in the field. Found by a cross-family review seat reading the CURED pages, not by any predicate in this lane: an invitation carries no percentage and no openness word, so neither `editorial_record_conformance` (which needs an openness claim beside a national-scope word) nor L10 (which needs a number) can see it. Ten of the twenty-five sit on codes this lane had already declared cured.

Four did worse than invite: they named BALI as the obstacle and pointed the reader at another province — on codes closed NATIONALLY. `10722` did it while `l4_bali.blocked` is False, i.e. it invented the local restriction it blamed. `22121` called itself 'one of the doors that stays open in Bali' at a 0% ceiling.

The sixteen government codes name their PRIVATE SIBLING, which is the actual answer to the question the reader is asking — `85315` is closed, `85316` (Pendidikan Menengah Atas Umum Swasta) is 100% open. Every sibling is asserted 100%/TERBUKA and has its title read from the dataset before it is named; a code printed in client copy is a claim. `84146` is the one government code with no private equivalent, and says so.

NOT included: `99000`, which the selection predicate flagged and which is already correct — it says in terms that the code is 'not for private foreign entrepreneurs seeking to set up a company in Bali'. The probe over-matched; the text is right, and it is left untouched rather than rewritten to match a pattern (W107: the probe that measures a disease can carry it).

Two findings from the cross-family grader (Codex GPT-5.6) changed the copy: `59121` said 'state bodies AND THE ENTITIES THEY MANDATE', a class the record does not name (its judul is 'oleh Pemerintah'); and `85315` offered an 'accreditation agreement' as an operating route, which is not what accreditation is. Both are gone — the second replaced by the sibling code, which is a fact rather than a paraphrase of one.

whoThisIsFor.old_excerpt: A foreign entrepreneur aiming to produce and sell traditional Indonesian pindang fish products, typically for domestic distribution.
whoThisIsFor.new: Indonesian-owned processors of pindang fish. The activity is reserved to cooperatives and Indonesian MSMEs by Perpres 49/2021, so foreign shareholding is 0% and a PT PMA cannot register it anywhere in Indonesia — the reservation is national, and moving the company to another province does not lift it. A foreign food business's route here is as a buyer or distributor of a domestic producer's output, not as its owner.
